claims.text: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large magnetocaloric and barocaloric response.
The unchanged alloy has poor structural integrity and is prone to cracking.
Cracking in the unchanged alloy is caused by a continuous brittle phase.
Approximately 4–5 at% Cr should be introduced substitutionally for an unspecified constituent.
A 4–5 at% Cr addition will induce a secondary Laves-type phase.
The Cr-induced secondary phase will be ductile.
The secondary phase will form a reticulated morphology that interrupts the continuous brittle matrix.
The secondary phase will occur as fine, discrete precipitates along grain boundaries or within the microstructure.
Chromium shifts phase equilibria toward precipitation of the proposed secondary phase.
The secondary phase will reduce the connectivity of the brittle matrix.
The secondary phase will enhance dislocation mobility.
The Cr-induced microstructure will mitigate crack propagation.
The Cr-modified alloy will have approximately 20–30% greater strength than the unchanged alloy.
The Cr-modified alloy will have greater fracture strain than the unchanged alloy.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain at least 90% of the unchanged alloy's caloric entropy change.
The Cr-induced secondary phase will preserve the magnetostructural transition responsible for the caloric response.
The proposed improvement will persist under moderate applied magnetic or pressure fields, caloric cycling temperatures, and quasi-static mechanical loading.
Significant changes in processing or composition may alter phase stability and the balance between caloric and mechanical performance.

contradictions.description: The secondary phase is described both as a reticulated network and as finely dispersed, discrete precipitates. These are materially different morphologies and imply different ways of interrupting matrix continuity.
